counterfactuals.prompt:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $3\text{rd}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$
counterfactuals.solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $3\text{rd}$ rows of $A$ are $2,$ $-3,$ and $4$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $2+(-3)+4=3.$
